submission.natural_language_explanation: N2423+ is a token-identity detector for a small, closed lexical cluster of information-source / news-attribution words: it fires on the word forms ' media/Media', ' net/Net', ' source(s)/Sources', ' press', ' text(s)', ' official(s)', ' main' and ' technical' wherever they occur (surrounding context shifts strength only mildly), and drops to exactly zero on every other token, including close synonyms such as 'newspaper', 'internet', 'journalist', 'website', 'report', 'wire', 'publication' and 'broadcast'. Words that fill the same news-attribution slots ('police', 'authorities', 'chief', 'staff', 'system', 'kernel', 'images', 'graphics', 'web', 'http') give a much weaker response (roughly 0.2-1.1 versus 1.3-3.3), so the pole is a lexical detector for the media/source/attribution vocabulary, not a semantic category detector.
